source_evidence: This fee subtracts a set percentage from any gain in the index. It is sometimes called the “margin,” “spread,” “asset fee,” or “administrative fee.”
answer: A spread is a percentage deducted from an index gain when the annuity calculates the return credited to your contract. For example, if the index gain is 9% and the spread is 3%, the credited return is 6%. This deduction can reduce your return much like a direct fee, even if the annuity is described as having “no fee.”
